associations.rationale: The type defines the contraction operator used in the spinor construction, not a semisimplicity or irreducible-classification conclusion.
The type defines the creation operator used in the hinted representation, so it is construction-level evidence only.
The type constructs an even-dimensional Clifford action on the spinor space but does not itself state the classification or semisimplicity claim.
The bijective even spin representation directly identifies the Clifford algebra with the full endomorphism algebra, stating the even matrix-algebra conclusion.
The type directly states irreducibility of the even spinor module for a nondegenerate form of dimension 2n.
The type directly states that every irreducible module in even dimension is isomorphic to the spinor module, giving uniqueness.
The type directly states that the even-dimensional Clifford algebra is a matrix algebra on a space of dimension 2^n.
The type constructs the spin action for a special hyperbolic form, a proof-strategy ingredient rather than the general source conclusion.
The type proves bijectivity only for the special hyperbolic model, serving as a prerequisite for the general even-dimensional result.
The type proves irreducibility only for the special hyperbolic spinor model, so it is helper evidence for the general claim.
The type directly states that the Clifford algebra is semisimple exactly when the symmetric bilinear form is nondegenerate.
The type directly states the requested nondegenerate-implies-semisimple assertion.
The type constructs the minus odd spin representation but does not itself assert its irreducibility, uniqueness, or the algebra decomposition.
The type constructs the plus odd spin representation, which is a construction used to prove the stated classification.
The printed type asserts IsSimpleModule for Spinor n, but the minus module action is hidden, so it does not directly state irreducibility of S-.
The printed type asserts IsSimpleModule for Spinor n, but the plus module action is hidden, so it does not directly state irreducibility of S+.
The empty equivalence type directly states that the two odd spinor representations are nonisomorphic.
The type directly states that every odd-dimensional irreducible is isomorphic to one of the two spinors.
The type directly identifies the odd-dimensional Clifford algebra with a product of two matrix algebras on spaces of dimension 2^n.
The type shows a nondegenerate B', surjective φ, and kernel equal to the Jacobson radical, but φ's codomain is elided, so the quotient identification is not directly displayed.
